Build layers for a nearest-neighbour map

Source: R/map.R
build_nearest_layers.Rd

Finds the nearest target features for each source feature, retains only matched targets, and constructs one connector line per match. This supports custom map renderers that need the same layers as map_nearest().

Usage

build_nearest_layers(source, target, k = 1, max_dist_km = NULL)

Arguments

source

An sf object of source point geometries.

target

An sf object of candidate point or polygon geometries.

k

Integer. Number of nearest targets per source. Defaults to 1; Inf may be used with max_dist_km for a radius search.

max_dist_km

Numeric or NULL. If set, omit targets farther than this distance in kilometres.

Value

A named list with four elements: source, the original source layer; matched_target, the target features present in the matches; connectors, an sf layer of connector lines or NULL when there are no matches; and table, the tibble returned by nearest().

See also

Other app support interfaces: extract_polygon_collection(), guess_name_col(), layer_id_col(), render_postal_reproducer_script(), render_reproducer_script()

Examples

stations <- retrieve_monitoring_stations_simple()
build_nearest_layers(stations[1:3, ], stations[4:10, ])
